cards.text: Psalm 125 is a song of ascents about people who trust in the LORD, and it says they're like Mount Zion. A MOUNTAIN, friend! The biggest thing anybody ever compared me to was a cookie.

cards.question: What does the psalm say about Mount Zion that makes it a picture of people who trust the LORD?
The psalm says Mount Zion lasts only for a season.

cards.text: Next picture: the mountains surround Jerusalem. Look left, mountain. Look right, MOUNTAIN. Turn ALL the way around, friend, still mountain.

cards.question: Just as the mountains surround Jerusalem, the LORD surrounds His ___.
How long does the psalm say the LORD surrounds His people?

answers.text: As long as the city stands

cards.text: Next the psalm says the scepter of the wicked will not rest upon the land allotted to the righteous. If I ever held a scepter, I'd grab it with my mustache and knock my OWN hat clean off.

cards.question: Why won't the scepter of the wicked rest on the land allotted to the righteous?

answers.text: So the righteous won't turn to injustice
So the righteous can grow their harvest
So the wicked will turn and repent

cards.text: Then the song turns and speaks straight to the LORD about the upright in heart. Upright, friend? I'm only upright because my gold base does all the work.

cards.question: The psalm speaks to the LORD about the upright in heart. What does it ask Him to do for them?

cards.text: Then the flip side: some people turn to crooked ways. You know when you miss your exit and the GPS says "recalculating" like it's tired of you?

cards.question: The psalm says the LORD will banish those who turn to crooked ways along with the evildoers.

cards.text: And the very last line is a blessing: "Peace be upon Israel." PEACE, friend! Back in the junk drawer, peace was the five minutes the dead batteries I shared it with stopped arguing over who had the most charge left.
